title: Compliance: dos, don'ts and the final check
objectives: Apply the module's compliance rules to any debt explanation.
Pass the trainer's final check: explain the price–yield seesaw, duration, the three debt risks and the PRC matrix without notes.
body_md:
Do: explain the three debt risks before recommending any debt product. Match fund duration to the client's goal date, and record why. Show YTM as an indicative figure, before expenses, never as a promised return. Check the riskometer and PRC cell against the client's risk profile. Disclose costs, exit loads and lock-ins in rupees. Refer tax questions to the client's CA. Recommend direct bonds only through SEBI-registered platforms or brokers.

- Don’t — Call any debt fund “safe”, “guaranteed” or “like an FD”.
- Don’t — Sell a high-yield or credit risk fund on yield alone.
- Don’t — Recommend AT1 or perpetual bonds to clients who need their capital back.
- Don’t — Put a large share of a client's money in one issuer.
- Don’t — Predict interest-rate moves as a reason to buy.
- Don’t — Quote small-savings or FD rates from memory; check the current rate.

> **Investor takeaway:** Mandatory line on all investor material: Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks. Read all scheme-related documents carefully. Final check for trainers: a new joiner passes this module when they can explain the price–yield seesaw, duration, the three debt risks and the PRC matrix to a first-time investor without notes.
example: A trainee explains, without notes: prices fall when rates rise; duration 4 means about −4% for +1% rates; the three risks are rate, credit and liquidity; A-I is the most conservative PRC cell.
say: Show YTM as indicative, before expenses, never as a promised return.
Match duration to the goal date, and record why.
never: Call a debt fund safe or like an FD.
Predict rate moves as a reason to buy.

check.q: Which of these is compliant when explaining a debt fund?
o: Show YTM as an indicative figure, before expenses, never as a promised return
Call the fund safe like an FD
Sell a credit risk fund on yield alone
Predict a rate cut to justify buying
check.why: Show YTM as an indicative figure, before expenses, never as a promised return.

check.why: Final check: explain the price–yield seesaw, duration, the three debt risks and the PRC matrix to a first-time investor without notes.
